subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a compaction-threshold flush-then-reset policy now that compaction and memoryFlush model overrides are shipped, and what privacy, provider, timeout, and session-state semantics should it use?
rationale: The remaining request changes config surface, silent model execution, durable memory writes, and session reset behavior; source inspection cannot safely choose those product and security defaults.

options.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset mode with #45608 so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

options.title: Add default-off resetAfterFlush
options.body: Approve a narrow default-off memoryFlush.resetAfterFlush mode with explicit provider, timeout, notification, and regression proof requirements.

options.title: Reject automatic reset after flush
options.body: Keep compaction as the canonical context-preservation path and rely on model overrides, memory flush, and manual reset flows for cost control.

recommendation.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset mode with #45608 so explicit, daily, idle, and compaction-pressure resets share one bounded policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across pre-compaction memory flush, memoryFlush.model, and reset policy behavior.
